title: Photo Upload Audit
user: iPhone and Android owners who auto-back up photos but need proof that every original, Live Photo sidecar, and video reached their chosen disk or server.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The author describes the common iPhone storage problem: no Mac, unwillingness to pay for iCloud, and unsafe manual folder-by-folder copying to an external drive.
33 reactions for a force-rescan-and-compare request after regularly occurring missing-photo uploads; users want a local/remote inventory comparison.

recurrence: Two 2025 communities identify the same failure mode: automated-looking photo backup with no trustworthy completeness check; lost originals are high severity.
current_workaround: Manually compare folders, trust a sync badge, or re-copy an entire camera roll.
incumbents_and_gap: iCloud Photos, Google Photos, Nextcloud, Immich, and Syncthing move files, but do not provide a simple portable receipt that explains missing originals, Live Photo pairs, and checksum mismatches across arbitrary destinations.
smallest_useful_product: Offline desktop/PWA scanner that reads a camera export and destination, matches hashes plus Live Photo pairs, and produces a missing/duplicate/changed report. Non-goals: photo hosting, cloud sync, facial recognition, or deletion automation.
success_measure: In a pilot set of 100,000 media files, users reconcile 99.9% of source files and identify every intentionally removed test file in one scan.
monetization: one-time — a privacy-preserving archival verification task is episodic and should work without an account.
constraints: Local-only indexing by default; never modify media; understand HEIC/MOV Live Photo pairing and filesystem timestamp differences; hashes can take substantial time on large libraries.
why_distinct: It verifies a backup handoff rather than becoming another photo library or sync service.

title: Statement Reconcile Bridge
user: People who keep a private budget spreadsheet or local ledger and need to reconcile a downloaded bank statement without surrendering transactions to an aggregator.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The asker says they quit popular finance apps because of paywalls, bloated upsell-oriented UX, manual syncing, and multiple disconnected tools.
Actual Budget's rule-action templating request has 20 reactions, showing active demand to transform transaction fields as part of a personal-finance workflow.

recurrence: Independent personal-finance users want local control while still needing repeatable transaction cleanup and reconciliation; monthly statement work is recurring and error-prone.
current_workaround: Download CSV/OFX, hand-normalize merchant strings in a spreadsheet, and visually search for duplicates against a ledger.
incumbents_and_gap: YNAB, Monarch, Copilot, Actual Budget, and Excel offer pieces of the workflow; none is a small neutral file-to-file reconciliation bridge that leaves the primary ledger where it already lives.
smallest_useful_product: Local PWA that imports CSV/OFX/QIF and an existing ledger CSV, applies explainable normalization rules, proposes one-to-one matches, and exports only reviewed rows plus an audit report. Non-goals: bank login, budgeting advice, investments, or cloud storage.
success_measure: A user reconciles a monthly statement with at least 95% automatic high-confidence matches and reviews the remainder in under 15 minutes.
monetization: one-time — handling financial files locally is more credible without a subscription or aggregation mandate.
constraints: No bank credential collection; parse untrusted files defensively; disclose that matches are suggestions and keep immutable import/audit records locally.
why_distinct: The product is a portable reconciliation handoff, not a replacement budget app.

title: ICS Intake Checker
user: People receiving event files from schools, clinics, conferences, and vendors who need to safely preview, fix, and route an .ics file before it pollutes the wrong calendar.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The thread documents iOS Calendar's awkward .ics intake path: Files, browser, share sheet, and Calendar itself cannot reliably import a saved calendar file.
A 2025 Lobsters discussion of gcal-sync reflects the continuing need to move events across calendar systems rather than treating calendar data as portable by default.

recurrence: Calendar-file import and cross-calendar sync remain separate user-facing problems across mobile and self-hosted communities; a malformed recurrence or timezone affects every invitee.
current_workaround: Email the file to oneself, add a subscription URL, edit raw ICS by hand, or import into a throwaway calendar first.
incumbents_and_gap: Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook, and CalDAV clients import or subscribe, but they expose little preflight explanation of timezone, recurrence, attendee, alarm, and duplicate risks.
smallest_useful_product: Browser-local drag-and-drop ICS inspector with readable event preview, timezone/recurrence validation, duplicate fingerprinting, and calendar-specific export choices. Non-goals: calendar hosting, scheduling links, or account sync.
success_measure: At least 90% of supplied problematic ICS fixtures receive a precise, actionable warning before import, with no event content sent off-device.
monetization: free — interoperability utilities benefit from open fixtures and broad adoption.
constraints: ICS parsing must tolerate vendor quirks and untrusted attachment data; do not contact embedded URLs automatically; preserve privacy of attendee information.
why_distinct: It is a calendar-file preflight and repair utility, not another calendar interface.

title: Friend File Drop
user: People sending a few private files to friends or family on mixed devices who need a linkless, low-friction transfer with a clear receipt that it finished.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN explicitly asks what people use to send files to friends who do not have AirDrop.
The 2025 Lobsters discussion is specifically about why cloud file sharing remains difficult, despite many established services.

recurrence: Cross-platform friend-to-friend transfer remains a direct 2025–26 request; the pain is highest when recipients cannot install the sender's preferred ecosystem app.
current_workaround: Use AirDrop only where possible, upload to Drive/Dropbox/WeTransfer, send a chat attachment, or compress and email files.
incumbents_and_gap: AirDrop, LocalSend, PairDrop, Dropbox Transfer, and WeTransfer are useful, but recipients still encounter app installs, link expiry ambiguity, size limits, or no sender-side completion receipt.
smallest_useful_product: A browser-based WebRTC transfer room with a six-word code, explicit file manifest and hash, resumable same-LAN fallback, and a sender/receiver completion receipt. Non-goals: persistent cloud storage, social accounts, or content discovery.
success_measure: At least 80% of first-time mixed-device transfers complete without either participant creating an account or installing an app.
monetization: free — trust and network effects matter more than a paywall; optional paid relay bandwidth can follow.
constraints: Use an opt-in relay only when direct WebRTC fails; disclose that metadata reaches the relay; scan neither content nor contacts; rate-limit abuse.
why_distinct: The compact transfer receipt and no-account mixed-device handoff are the product, not another cloud drive.

title: Bookmark Freshness Review
user: Researchers and professionals with years of saved links who need to decide what is dead, duplicated, paywalled, changed, or still worth keeping without uploading their bookmark archive.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The 94-comment Ask HN thread asks whether people still bookmark websites after services such as Delicious and Pocket disappeared or degraded.
226 reactions on assigning a bookmark to a browser container demonstrate that a saved URL often needs operational context, not merely a title and folder.

recurrence: The HN discussion has broad participation and the browser issue has long-lived demand: bookmarks persist, but their intent and safe context decay.
current_workaround: Leave a growing archive untouched, use folders/tags manually, or migrate between bookmark services after one shuts down.
incumbents_and_gap: Browser bookmark managers, Raindrop.io, Pinboard, and Linkding organize links, but do not make periodic offline review of link health, duplicates, archive captures, and required browser context the central workflow.
smallest_useful_product: Local browser extension that imports HTML bookmarks, checks status and canonical duplicates on demand, groups stale candidates, stores a short user-written purpose/context note, and exports standard HTML. Non-goals: hosted sync, AI summaries, or scraping paywalled pages.
success_measure: In a 30-day pilot, users archive, repair, or deliberately retain at least 20% of bookmarks older than two years while exporting a portable archive.
monetization: one-time — personal archives should remain usable if a service closes.
constraints: Never transmit the archive by default; throttle link checks and honor site limits; clearly distinguish a failed request from a dead page.
why_distinct: It is an intentional decay-management pass for a local archive, not a social read-later clone.

title: Docx Markdown Fidelity Report
user: Teams inheriting Word-heavy documentation who need to convert it to Markdown while knowing exactly which tables, tracked changes, comments, images, and styles need human review.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The asker inherited an ingestion pipeline that converts Word to PDF and then PDF to Markdown, and questions the quality and necessity of that lossy chain.
A 53-reaction export request describes multi-document publishing workflows, a reminder that conversion must preserve a document set's structure rather than only emit text.

recurrence: A current migration question and sustained export-workflow demand point to document conversion being a handoff problem: users need confidence in exceptions, not just an output file.
current_workaround: Run Pandoc or LibreOffice, inspect output manually, and discover broken tables or omitted comments after publishing.
incumbents_and_gap: Pandoc, LibreOffice, Mammoth, and cloud converters produce Markdown; they do not lead with a reviewable fidelity ledger for risky Word constructs across a batch.
smallest_useful_product: Local CLI that converts DOCX directly to Markdown and emits a per-file fidelity report listing tables, comments, revisions, embedded objects, footnotes, styles, and image extraction outcomes. Non-goals: OCR, document editing, PDF round-tripping, or hosted conversion.
success_measure: For a curated corpus of complex DOCX files, every unsupported or lossy construct is reported with its source location before the output is accepted.
monetization: one-time — migration teams can buy a dependable local review tool for a bounded project.
constraints: Treat documents as untrusted; do not execute embedded content; preserve filenames safely; license any conversion library compatibly.
why_distinct: The deliverable is a conversion-risk handoff report, not another generic document converter.

title: Trip Plan Handoff Pack
user: A trip organizer who needs to give companions a dependable, printable/offline itinerary with reservations, timezone-safe meeting points, expenses, and change ownership.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The travel-planner request explicitly lists itinerary management, budget tracking, multi-currency support, location suggestions, and packing needs in one workflow.
The Linkal discussion shows a distinct community working on calendar aggregation, relevant because travel plans routinely span externally maintained calendars.

recurrence: Planning requirements combine itinerary, money, and calendar data; the unresolved failure is distributing one current plan to people with different apps and intermittent connectivity.
current_workaround: Share a Google Doc, chat screenshots, booking emails, several calendar invites, and a separate expense-split app.
incumbents_and_gap: TripIt, Wanderlog, Google Maps, Splitwise, and calendars each hold part of the plan; none emphasizes an owner-controlled, offline handoff pack with provenance and a concise change log.
smallest_useful_product: Local-first web app that imports ICS and reservation emails pasted by the user, creates a timezone-normalized itinerary, exports a signed offline HTML/PDF pack and change summary. Non-goals: booking travel, recommendations, social feed, or payment collection.
success_measure: A group of four can retrieve the current itinerary, next meeting point, and reservation reference offline from a shared pack in under 30 seconds.
monetization: one-time — trip planning is episodic and an offline export is the durable value.
constraints: Do not access email accounts; redact confirmation codes in shared exports on request; clarify that imported times and carrier changes require user verification.
why_distinct: It creates an accountable group handoff artifact rather than an AI travel recommender or booking site.

title: Private Caption Export
user: Hearing-impaired professionals and privacy-conscious teams who need searchable local meeting captions and an accessible handoff of only the agreed excerpts.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A hearing-impaired engineer asks about demand for local-first live transcription, explaining that local processing avoids workplace privacy concerns while serving meetings and interviews.
A 2026 accessibility discussion focuses on making accessibility measurable and accountable rather than treating it as a vague promise.

recurrence: The direct accessibility user request and the newer accountability discussion support a focused gap: captions must be private, usable in the moment, and exportable as a responsible handoff.
current_workaround: Use Otter/Teams/Zoom cloud transcripts, record everything, or manually type notes and redact them later.
incumbents_and_gap: Otter, Zoom, Teams, macOS Live Captions, and Whisper tools provide capture; few make it simple to keep audio local, mark consent boundaries, and export selected accessible notes with timestamps and speakers uncertainly labeled.
smallest_useful_product: Offline desktop wrapper around an on-device speech model that displays live captions, lets the user mark/share only selected spans, and exports accessible HTML/TXT with timestamps. Non-goals: cloud transcription, surveillance recording, speaker identification, or meeting bots.
success_measure: A user can produce an accessible, redactable excerpt from a 30-minute local recording with no network connection and no raw audio leaving the device.
monetization: one-time — privacy-sensitive assistive software should continue working without a transcript subscription.
constraints: Obtain consent and follow recording laws; ship model/license notices; distinguish uncertain text; minimize retained audio and provide secure local deletion.
why_distinct: It is an accessibility and consent-aware excerpt handoff tool, not a generic meeting-summary wrapper.

title: Chore Load Ledger
user: Households sharing recurring work who need a neutral record of what was agreed, completed, skipped, and handed over without turning home life into surveillance.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ask HN explicitly asks for people's best household-chore tips, indicating recurring coordination and motivation difficulty rather than a one-off task list need.
The open feature request to assign owners to chores has 14 reactions, supporting demand for explicit responsibility in household automation tooling.

recurrence: Household coordination appears in a 2025 community question and in a reacted feature request; unclear ownership creates recurring resentment, not merely missed reminders.
current_workaround: Use a whiteboard, shared notes, nagging messages, or a gamified chore app that tracks points but loses the actual handoff context.
incumbents_and_gap: Tody, Sweepy, Nipto, Todoist, and Home Assistant chore helpers schedule work; they under-serve lightweight agreement records, temporary handoffs, and equitable load review without scores or surveillance.
smallest_useful_product: Private shared PWA with recurring chores, explicit owner/backup/definition-of-done, handoff notes, and a weekly time/load ledger. Non-goals: child scoring, location tracking, public leaderboards, or smart-home control.
success_measure: After four weeks, every recurring chore has a current owner or handoff and households report fewer than one ownership dispute per week in pilot feedback.
monetization: one-time — a small household utility should not monetize behavioral data or impose a recurring fee.
constraints: End-to-end encrypted sync if sync is offered; support export/delete; avoid manipulative streaks and gamification aimed at children.
why_distinct: The core is a humane responsibility handoff ledger rather than another rewards-based chore chart.

title: Next Step Card
user: People with ADHD overwhelmed by a large task list who need one reversible, explainable next action without having their life data profiled by an AI service.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The builder says decision-making over many tasks is the problem and asks what an ADHD to-do app should do beyond ranking tasks by deadline, value, and difficulty.
The Lobsters productivity discussion provides an independent technical-community context for skepticism about productivity systems that add process rather than reduce friction.

recurrence: The current direct request is specific about decision paralysis; the conservative product scope avoids assuming a universal productivity method.
current_workaround: Keep many competing lists, use priority formulas, ask another person to choose, or abandon a complex planner when it becomes another task.
incumbents_and_gap: Todoist, Things, TickTick, Sunsama, and ADHD-focused planners manage lists and schedules; they commonly expand into full planning systems rather than offering a privacy-preserving one-card decision aid with an undo trail.
smallest_useful_product: Offline mobile PWA that accepts a small task inbox, asks for energy/time/deadline constraints, shows one next-step card with its rule explanation, and supports defer/break-down/ask-for-help. Non-goals: diagnosis, therapy, coaching, calendar replacement, or LLM chat.
success_measure: In a two-week diary study, participants start a suggested task within ten minutes at least 50% more often than from an unfiltered list.
monetization: one-time — users should retain access to their support tool without a subscription or behavioral-data business model.
constraints: Make no medical claims; all scoring must be inspectable and adjustable; protect sensitive task content locally; offer accessibility-friendly reduced-motion and large-text modes.
why_distinct: It narrows the job to selecting an explainable next physical step, not building another planner or thin LLM coach.

title: Local Finance Export Vault
user: Privacy-minded individuals moving between budgeting tools who need to preserve and inspect their own financial exports before an app, pricing tier, or sync service changes.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A privacy-first budgeting tool proposal explicitly keeps financial data in IndexedDB/localStorage with no account or Plaid integration, validating local-only handling as a user-facing requirement.
An Actual Budget feedback issue with 11 reactions and a 2026 update describes recurring requests around making personal-finance data understandable, rather than merely storing transactions.

recurrence: Separate personal-finance discussions show friction with feature-heavy apps and a continuing demand for data that remains local; portability is most urgent when users switch tools.
current_workaround: Export CSVs into ad-hoc folders, trust a vendor export, or flatten data into a spreadsheet and lose categories, accounts, and reconciliation metadata.
incumbents_and_gap: YNAB, Monarch, Actual, Tiller, and spreadsheets provide exports or storage, but do not offer a vendor-neutral local archive that validates completeness and records the meaning of each column/category mapping.
smallest_useful_product: Offline vault that imports common budget exports, snapshots an immutable manifest and hashes, maps fields into a documented neutral schema, and produces a readable migration packet. Non-goals: account aggregation, spending advice, bank connectivity, or multi-user cloud sync.
success_measure: A user can import two exports from different tools and produce a validated archive plus field-mapping report without any financial row leaving the device.
monetization: one-time — data portability is an episodic, trust-sensitive utility.
constraints: Encrypt local archive option; no credentials; transparent schema versioning; never claim regulatory-grade accounting or tax correctness.
why_distinct: It protects an exit-ready personal data archive rather than competing to be the user's finance dashboard.

title: PDF Accessibility Preflight
user: Small organizations publishing PDFs who need a simple local preflight that identifies the accessibility failures most likely to block a reader before upload.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The asker seeks practical experience choosing website accessibility tools such as WAVE and axe rather than relying on a marketing promise.
The open request for tagged-PDF/PDF-UA support has 33 reactions and calls out PDF accessibility as a concrete missing capability.

recurrence: Accessibility-tool selection and a reacted tagged-PDF request show that people need actionable checks, while full enterprise accessibility suites are often too broad for a publish-time gate.
current_workaround: Use Acrobat's checker if available, run a generic web scanner after publishing, or rely on manual visual inspection.
incumbents_and_gap: Adobe Acrobat, PAC, axesPDF, and enterprise accessibility platforms are capable but can be expensive or specialist-heavy; a small team needs a local prioritized report that explains the first fixes without claiming certification.
smallest_useful_product: Local CLI/web app that inspects PDF structure, tags, reading order clues, title/language, images without alt text, and contrast heuristics; emits a human-review checklist. Non-goals: automated remediation, legal certification, OCR, or document hosting.
success_measure: Against a fixture set of known accessible/inaccessible PDFs, the tool flags 95% of deliberately introduced structural failures and produces no claim of conformance.
monetization: free — transparent local checks and public test fixtures improve accessibility adoption; paid support can follow.
constraints: Do not represent heuristic results as WCAG/PDF-UA certification; process documents locally; account for encrypted PDFs and malformed files safely; consult accessibility experts on rules.
why_distinct: It is a narrowly scoped, honest publish-time preflight rather than an accessibility-overlay dark pattern or full PDF editor.
